Hise was a primary sponsor of SB 352, Restore Confidence in Government. Part 1 requires every in-person voter to show valid photo ID, lists accepted photo IDs (including a state voter ID card), requires a photocopy of photo ID or a utility bill or similar document with a mail-in absentee ballot for some voters, and lets a voter without the required ID vote a provisional ballot. Bill text at https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2011/Bills/Senate/PDF/S352v0.pdf. Date is the first reading; the bill was then referred to committee.
subjects: provisional ballot for voter without ID

findings.note: Hise was a primary sponsor of SB 747, Elections Law Changes (filed 2023-06-01; became Session Law 2023-140). The final law text at https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2023/Bills/Senate/PDF/S747v6.pdf has same-day registrants present photo ID, requires a photocopy of ID or an ID affidavit with absentee ballots, lists a driver license, state ID or last four Social Security digits for an absentee request, and has the State Board check the citizenship status of people removed from jury lists as non-citizens.
Hise is listed among the ayes (30 to 19) on the Senate vote to override the governor's veto of SB 747, Elections Law Changes. The roll call lists Hise as the bill's sponsor.

findings.passage: I have fought to protect our elections from further fraud by passing legislation like SB725 which prohibits big tech from giving money to boards of elections.
findings.note: Hise's campaign home page, under the heading PROTECT OUR ELECTIONS. The page is undated; its footer reads Copyright 2022. It names a law on private money for election boards and does not mention ID. Saved as an election-integrity statement.

findings.passage: During my time there I have fought to lower taxes, secure elections, and end the teaching of Critical Race Theory in schools.
findings.note: Quote from Hise on his campaign home page, where he lists securing elections among his priorities. Page undated; footer reads Copyright 2022. It does not mention ID.

findings.passage: Senator Hise sponsored a hugely popular measure requiring voters to show photo identification at the polls. Studies show photo ID requirements boost voter confidence and participation. Gov. Perdue later vetoed the voter ID legislation.
findings.note: Text from the Voter identification section of Hise's 2014 campaign website, as quoted in the 2014 section of Ballotpedia's page (Ballotpedia says the campaign site highlighted these issues). The original campaign page is now a 404, so this is the Ballotpedia copy. It is third-person campaign wording, not a first-person quote.

findings.passage: “Nothing suppresses the votes of racial minorities more than their votes being canceled by someone who votes illegally,” Hise said. “I am fighting today to protect the vote of every North Carolinian.”
findings.note: Quoted by Carolina Journal (Dan Way) during Senate debate on the photo ID constitutional amendment, answering the argument that voter ID suppresses minority votes.

findings.passage: “They’ll tell you how elections were stole, how ballots were sold for half pints of liquor, how they used to carry blank ballots out and pay people when they left, and sent marked ballots back in,” Hise said.
findings.note: Quoted by Carolina Journal; Hise describes historical stories of vote fraud in his region as a reason for the photo ID amendment.

findings.passage: “Our hope is that this will restore some confidence in many citizens in their voting process,” said Mitchell County Republican Sen. Ralph Hise, of Mitchell County, according to The Associated Press.
findings.note: Spectrum News 1 quoting Hise (via AP) on the 2023 omnibus election bill, which changed mail-ballot receipt rules and added signature-verification pilots.

Hise is first-listed primary sponsor of S921 (SL 2024-58), a constitutional amendment to require photographic identification from all voters, not only in-person voters, put to voters on Nov 3, 2026. Filed Dec 2, 2024; ratified Dec 13, 2024. Bill text fetched from the NC General Assembly PDF.
Hise is listed among the Ayes on the Senate third reading of S921, the all-voters photo ID constitutional amendment; the roll call lists him as sponsor.

Hise and Daniel are primary sponsors of S214, Ensure Orderly 2019 Elections (SL 2019-4, effective March 14, 2019), which lets any registered voter voting in person in 2019 vote an official ballot whether or not photo ID is presented, and keeps implementation and education work going. Summary text from the NC House summary page.
